brief.subject: Diesel dips to $6.292, truck jobs flat, Mexico trade record
brief.headline: Diesel Eases 6 Cents as Trucking Jobs Hold Steady and Mexico Trade Hits a Record
brief.dek: Diesel slips to $6.292, October trucking payrolls stay flat, Mexico cross-border trade sets a record, and container imports climb 9%.
brief.lede: Diesel fell 6.0 cents to $6.292 a gallon this week, a small break for carriers still paying 9.3 cents more than four weeks ago.

sections.heading: Diesel Takes a Small Step Back
bullets: $6.292 per gallon is the U.S. average retail diesel price for the week of 2026-11-02.
Down 6.0 cents (0.9%) from the prior week, a modest break at the pump.
Up 9.3 cents over four weeks, so fuel surcharges and lane quotes still need a close look.

sections.heading: Trucking Jobs Stall in October
bullets: October truck transportation employment was unchanged from September, per the Bureau of Labor Statistics.
September was revised down to 1,471,300 from 1,473,100, a sign the driver pool is not expanding.
Flat payrolls suggest capacity is holding steady rather than flooding back into the market.

sections.heading: Mexico Trade Booms, Theft Risk Grows
bullets: $96.3B in September trade set a record and widened Mexico's lead as the top U.S. trading partner.
Strong cross-border volume keeps freight moving through border lanes for carriers serving Mexico.
42% of Q3 cargo theft incidents in Mexico involved parked trucks, according to Overhaul.
Drivers running into Mexico should treat parking stops as the highest-risk part of the trip.

sections.heading: Import Freight Climbs as Prices Rise
bullets: 9% rise in North America container imports in September, despite disruptions and higher shipping costs.
More boxes arriving means more drayage and inland freight for carriers near ports.
Aurora's autonomous truck production is delayed by supply and quality issues, though it still targets more than 1,000 trucks by end of 2027.

sections.heading: Rail Fight Spills Into Public View
bullets: The STB rejected Union Pacific's appeal and ordered release of a video with an alleged rate hike threat.
The remarks targeted shippers opposed to the Norfolk Southern merger; UP's CEO now says he was joking.
Schneider National has shifted its intermodal partnership to Norfolk Southern, reshaping rail options shippers weigh against trucks.
